title: Continuo
subtitle: A Minecraft bot that walks to a block you mark

repo.read: tracked files only (git ls-files); nothing was built or run

statusMeaning.works: In the code, and the repository records tests or an in-game run for it.
statusMeaning.partial: In the code, but incomplete or never checked in a real game.
statusMeaning.planned: Described in the docs only; no code.
statusMeaning.unknown: Could not be determined from the repository.

docsVsCode: Search threading: mc-automation-architecture.md plans A* on a worker pool over a frozen world copy. The code runs the search on the game's main thread, 2,000 positions per tick (Run.java, SealedSnapshot.java).

Position correction: the architecture document and docs/injection-strategy.md plan a 'server moved you back' event needing bytecode injection. IGameEvents has only onClientTick; the walker re-finds its place on the route every tick instead (PathFollower.java).
Per-move executors: the architecture document gives each movement its own executor. The code has one walker that derives the move kind from each step (PathExecutor.java, MovementKind.java).
Capability negotiation: described as a three-way negotiation between game, player and settings. The code has a single caller-granted permission, PARKOUR (Capability.java).
Actuator surface: the document lists hotbar, item use and block breaking. IActuator has only setInput and setLook.
Sprint: MovementCosts.java prices every move at sprint speed and says the executor sprints; PathExecutor.java always writes SPRINT = false.

Module tree: the document's core-math, core-world, bridge, scripts and web-ui modules do not exist; the real modules are platform, core, core-movement, core-pathfinder, core-engine, movement-parkour, runtime, platform-testkit and two adapters.
The D2 spec's status line still reads 'design, for review' although the walker is merged (commit 55e0141).

elements.name: Proof and guard rails
elements.summary: Checks that run without the game and keep the bot's promises from eroding, plus one manual checklist.

elements.name: Reports raw block facts
elements.summary: Answers 'what is at this position' with the game's own facts and no judgement: id, collision boxes, fluid, climbable, falls.
elements.statusWhy: Both versions dumped and compared in a real client on 2026-08-15.
rules: Reports facts only; what a block means is decided elsewhere.
An unloaded or out-of-range position is reported as unreadable, never guessed.
May only be asked on the game's main thread while a world is loaded.
notes: On 1.7.10, collision boxes lose precision very far from the origin (around a million blocks out); the roadmap records this as untested.

elements.name: Reports where the player is
elements.summary: Gives the player's feet position, facing and on-ground flag for the current tick.
elements.statusWhy: Checked in both game versions on 2026-09-02.
rules: Height means the feet. On 1.7.10 that is the bottom of the collision box, not the game's own 'Y', which is 1.62 blocks higher.
Values describe this tick only and are never kept for the next.
Exactly six facts: x, y, z, yaw, pitch, on-ground. No velocity.

elements.name: Hears keys and ticks
elements.summary: Registers the four keys and forwards every game tick and key click into the bot, once per game version.
elements.statusWhy: Manual checklist passed on both versions (latest record 2026-08-15).

inside.name: Registers keys H K L J

rules: Wiring only: no decision about the bot's behaviour lives here.
Both halves of every tick are forwarded, start before end.
Forge 1.7.10 has no shutdown event, so that adapter never sends one; the contract allows it.

knobs.name: Default keys
knobs.value: H mark, K walk, L probe, J dump
knobs.effect: Change the default key for each action.

notes: For one tick after a world change, a walk-key press can still use a goal marked in the previous world; the code documents this and leaves it unfixed.

elements.name: Guards the game loop
elements.summary: Stands between the game's tick and the bot: lets ticks through only inside a loaded world, stops the bot on any world change, and contains crashes.
elements.statusWhy: Covered by a 28-case conformance suite, plus manual runs on both versions.
rules: A bot crash never reaches the game's own tick loop.
After a crash the bot is stopped and gets no ticks until the next world load.
The bot is ordered to stop on every change of loaded world: unload, dimension change, load.
No tick is delivered without a world and a player.
Tick-end is never delivered without its tick-start.
Key clicks made outside a world are thrown away, not replayed later.
The bot is started exactly once.

elements.name: Classifies blocks
elements.summary: Turns raw block facts into the bot's own vocabulary: a shape, the height of the top, a fluid, and tags such as 'avoid'.
elements.statusWhy: Headless tests; both versions agree on 27 of 27 compared fixture blocks.
rules: One classifier for every game version, so two versions cannot disagree about the same boxes.
A shape that fits no category exactly becomes 'partial', never the nearest category.
A malformed rule table fails loudly; an unknown game version simply gets no overrides.

knobs.name: Rule table rows
knobs.effect: Which blocks count as water, lava, harmful (avoid) or slowing.

knobs.name: THIN_LAYER_MAX
knobs.effect: How tall a layer may be and still count as carpet or snow.

notes: The tags 'slow', 'falling' and 'climbable' are produced, but nothing downstream reads them yet. Only 'avoid' changes a route.
Ice classifies exactly like stone: slipperiness is not modelled (the roadmap lists it as open).

elements.name: Remembers each block kind
elements.summary: Reads a position from the game and classifies each distinct kind of block only once per world.
rules: Its memory is wiped on every world change, because block numbers are only valid for one session.
An unreadable position comes back as 'unknown', never as nothing.

elements.name: Copies terrain it reads
elements.summary: Keeps a private copy of every position a search touches, so each is read from the game at most once per search.
rules: A copy is a point in time and is never refreshed; a route gone stale is caught by the walker, not here.
Filling happens only on the game's main thread.
A cancelled search drops its copy, so an old world is not kept alive.

knobs.name: BITS
knobs.effect: Size of a storage cell: a trade between speed and wasted memory.

notes: Docs differ: the architecture document plans searching on a worker thread against a frozen copy. The code rejected that after measuring it; the search runs on the main thread in slices, and sealing is used only by the route preview.
The 'does this copy cover a position' check exists but nothing uses it.

elements.name: Offers possible moves
elements.summary: From one position, lists every neighbour the player could reach and what each costs in game ticks.
elements.statusWhy: Headless tests, including an audit of every move's declared cost.
rules: Moves are offered in a fixed order, so the same world always gives the same route.
Each move declares its cheapest cost per block, and an audit checks that claim.
A diagonal step needs both corner columns clear at feet and head height.
A drop is never deeper than 3 blocks.
The gap jump is offered only when the caller grants the 'parkour' permission.

knobs.name: TRAVERSE
knobs.effect: Base cost of walking one block; every other cost builds on it.

knobs.name: JUMP_SURCHARGE
knobs.effect: Extra cost of a jump; makes the planner prefer flat ground.

knobs.name: MAX_SAFE_FALL
knobs.effect: Deepest drop the planner will take.

knobs.name: Built-in move order
knobs.effect: Decides which of two equally cheap routes wins.

notes: Costs are priced at sprint speed, but the walker never presses sprint.
Docs differ: the architecture document describes the game and the player negotiating abilities. In the code there is one ability, 'parkour', and the caller simply grants it or not.
The code says these costs are 'admissible and self-consistent, not validated' against a real walk.

elements.name: Judges where one can stand
elements.summary: Decides from a block's measured top whether a body can pass through it and whether it is a floor.
rules: A block that could not be read is never passable.
Fluids and harmful blocks are neither passable nor a floor: no swimming, no lava.
Standing needs two passable blocks above one floor block.
A fence is never a floor.

knobs.name: PASSABLE_MAX_TOP
knobs.effect: How tall a layer may be and still be walked through (carpet, snow).

knobs.name: SUPPORT_MIN_TOP
knobs.effect: How low a top may be and still count as a floor (admits farmland).

knobs.name: SUPPORT_MAX_TOP
knobs.effect: Anything taller is a fence or wall, not a floor.

elements.name: Searches for a route
elements.summary: An A* search over block positions toward a goal, spent in small slices so it never freezes the game.
elements.statusWhy: Headless tests on real terrain fixtures; the same route came back in a live client on 2026-09-02.
rules: The same world and the same start give the same route, exactly.
Cutting a search into slices never changes its answer.
The distance estimate must never overestimate, or routes stop being the shortest.
A search ends in exactly one of four ways: found, partial, no path, over budget.

knobs.name: DEFAULT_NODE_BUDGET
knobs.effect: How much one search may explore before it settles for a partial route.

knobs.name: DEFAULT_MIN_PROGRESS_BLOCKS
knobs.effect: How much closer a partial route must get to be worth walking.

notes: A second kind of goal, 'any height at this x and z', exists in code but nothing in the running bot uses it.

elements.name: Chains long routes
elements.summary: When one search runs out of budget, continues leg by leg from the closest point reached; also meters the work per tick.
elements.statusWhy: Headless tests; measured in a live client on 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02.
rules: Every leg must end about 4 blocks closer to the goal by the search's own estimate, which is why a run always ends.
'No path' is final: it proves the goal cannot be reached from here.
The end of a slice is not a result; it only means 'ask again next tick'.

knobs.name: SLICE_NODES
knobs.effect: Work done per tick: higher finds routes sooner but risks a visible hitch. Measured in game: worst slice 22.3 ms cold, 6 to 9 ms warm.

elements.name: Starts and stops walks
elements.summary: The bot's front door: accepts 'walk to this block', hands each tick to the walker, and stops everything on demand.
elements.statusWhy: Works behind a developer key only. Goals, priorities and commands are planned.
rules: An idle bot writes nothing at all, so it never fights the owner's own keyboard.
Stop releases held keys once and forgets every classified block.
Only the first half of a tick does work; the second half is ignored.
notes: The code calls this class 'the entire core, for now'.

elements.name: Steers along the route
elements.summary: Every tick, works out where the player is on the route and which keys to hold; searches ahead, replans, or gives up as needed.
elements.statusWhy: Built and unit-tested without the game. The in-game checklist steps for it (13 to 22) have never been run.
rules: Recomputed from scratch every tick: it remembers no key it pressed.
While walking, it states the full set of seven keys every tick.
Jump is pressed only for a step up, and only while on the ground.
Arrival means within half a block of the goal block.
'No path' ends the walk; it is not retried.
It never performs a gap jump, and stops if a route contains one.

knobs.name: PLAN_AHEAD_STEPS
knobs.effect: How close to the end of its route the walker starts searching for the next stretch.

knobs.name: STUCK_TICKS
knobs.effect: How long without progress before it replans.

knobs.name: MAX_CONSECUTIVE_REPATHS
knobs.effect: How many replans without progress before it gives up.

knobs.name: OFF_PATH_RADIUS
knobs.effect: How far from the route counts as 'pushed off' and triggers a replan.

knobs.name: ARRIVE_RADIUS
knobs.effect: How close to the goal counts as arrived.

knobs.name: W
knobs.effect: How far along the route it looks for the player's place; too large skips loops on spiral stairs.

notes: All six numbers above, and the turning speed next door, are marked 'extrapolated' in the code: reasoned, not yet measured in a game.
Docs differ: the architecture document and docs/injection-strategy.md plan a 'server moved you back' event. The code has no such event; finding its place again every tick replaced it.
Docs differ: the architecture document gives each move its own executor. The code has this one walker, which reads the kind of move off each step.

elements.name: Limits turning speed
elements.summary: Turns the player toward the wanted direction by at most 30 degrees per tick instead of snapping.
elements.statusWhy: Unit-tested; the in-game turning check (step 17) has never been run.
rules: Key presses pass through untouched; only turning is limited.
It keeps no memory: each tick it turns from the player's actual facing.

knobs.name: MAX_DEG_PER_TICK
knobs.effect: Turning speed: a half-turn takes about 0.3 s. Extrapolated, not measured.

elements.name: Presses keys, turns head
elements.summary: Sets the game's own movement keys and the player's look direction; the only way the bot touches the game.
elements.statusWhy: Key presses checked in both versions (2026-08-13); looking checked on 2026-09-02.
rules: Seven inputs exist and no more: forward, back, left, right, jump, sneak, sprint.
Pure translation: an input maps to one of the game's key bindings.
It works even when the owner has unbound that key.
Setting the look direction does nothing, silently, when there is no player.
notes: Docs differ: the architecture document also lists hotbar selection, item use and block breaking. None of those exist in code.

elements.name: Writes to the game log
elements.summary: Carries the bot's one-line explanations into the game's log file.

elements.name: Dumps a row of blocks
elements.summary: Writes the 32 blocks east of the player, raw facts plus classification, to a text file for comparing game versions.
rules: One line per position: index, block id, state, classified result.

knobs.name: Row length
knobs.effect: How many blocks one press dumps.

elements.name: Previews a route as text
elements.summary: Searches from the player to the marked goal without walking, then writes a text-art map and a one-line summary with timings.
elements.statusWhy: Run in a live client on 2026-08-31, and in both versions on 2026-09-02.
rules: Developer tool only: nothing calls it during a normal walk.
Time is reported and never used to stop a search.
A clipped map says that it was clipped.

knobs.name: NODE_BUDGET
knobs.effect: How far a preview may explore.

knobs.name: MAX_EXTENT
knobs.effect: Largest map it will draw.

notes: The preview grants the gap jump and the walker does not, so a previewed route can differ from the one actually walked.
Pressing the probe key during a walk gives spurious notices (documented as expected).

elements.name: Marks the goal
elements.summary: Remembers the block the player is standing on as the destination.
rules: A marked goal is dropped on any world or dimension change.
There is one goal at a time; marking again replaces it.
notes: The destination is kept by this inspection tool, not by the bot's core. A proper owner of goals is planned.

elements.name: Builds on every push
elements.summary: Runs the whole build, all tests and all checks on every push and pull request.
rules: The game adapters are built too, but have no automated tests; they cannot have any without the game.

elements.name: Keeps the core game-free
elements.summary: Fails the build if core code mentions Minecraft, uses anything newer than Java 8, or depends in the wrong direction.
rules: Eight modules are 'pure'; only the two adapters may touch the game.
Nothing may depend on an adapter.
The same core jar must load on a game from 2014 and one from 2025.

knobs.name: allowedProjectDependencies
knobs.effect: The only place where 'who may depend on whom' is written.

elements.name: Tests routes on text worlds
elements.summary: Runs the planner and the walker against worlds drawn as text, with no game present.
rules: Tests assert which route comes back, not merely that one exists.
Five terrain files were captured from a real world and are replayed as fixtures.

elements.name: Tests the safety gate
elements.summary: A 28-case suite that drives the safety gate with a fake game and a recording bot.
rules: A green suite says nothing about whether an adapter is wired to the right game objects; that is the manual checklist's job.

elements.name: Compares both versions' blocks
elements.summary: Diffs the block dumps from the two game versions and checks each against a human-reviewed golden file.
rules: Golden files are never regenerated by a key press, only by a line-by-line human review.
notes: Of 32 fixture blocks, 27 are compared across versions; 5 are excluded because the two games genuinely differ (carpet and farmland among them).
Agreement shows the two adapters match each other, not that the classification is right.

elements.name: Owner checks in game
elements.summary: A 22-step manual checklist a person runs in both game versions; the only evidence the adapters are wired correctly.
elements.statusWhy: Steps 1 to 12 are recorded as passing (2026-08-15, before the walker existed). Steps 13 to 22, which test the walker, have never been run.
rules: Never run 'gradlew clean': it deletes the decompiled game sources used to review adapter code.

elements.name: More game versions
elements.summary: Planned (milestone M9): further adapters such as NeoForge and 1.20.x, each a re-test of the game boundary.

elements.name: Browser control panel
elements.summary: Planned (M7, a separate repository): a web page for settings, route display and a packet timeline.

elements.name: Talks to outside programs
elements.summary: Planned (M6): a local, token-protected connection that streams the bot's state and accepts commands and settings.

elements.name: Takes goals and commands
elements.summary: Planned (M5, part D3): goals, a manager choosing among them, and a 'goto x y z' command.

elements.name: Runs tasks: mine, build
elements.summary: Planned (M8): scripts that set goals for the walker, such as mining a vein or building from a schematic.

elements.name: Flies and other moves
elements.summary: Planned (M10): elytra flight and modded movements, needing a richer notion of position.

routes.name: Mark a goal
routes.summary: Stand on a block and press H; the bot remembers that block as the destination.
stepNotes: The owner presses H.
The click is collected at the end of the tick.
The player's feet position is read.
That block becomes the goal, replacing any earlier one.

routes.name: Walk to a marked block
routes.summary: Press K and the bot plans a route to the marked block and walks it, turning gradually, until it stands on it.
routes.statusWhy: Built and unit-tested without the game. The repository's own checklist says the in-game steps for the walker have never been run, and its seven tuning numbers are still estimates.
stepNotes: The owner presses K.
The click rides in with the next tick.
The marked goal becomes a walk order.
The walker drops whatever it was doing and takes the destination.
It reads where the player is standing.
It asks for a route from there to the goal, with no gap jumps.
A search leg starts; 2,000 positions are explored per tick.
Blocks around the search are read from the game.
A kind of block seen for the first time is described in full.
It is classified once and remembered.
Each position read is copied, so it is read only once.
The search reads terrain from that copy.
Each candidate spot is judged: passable, a floor, standable.
Reachable neighbours come back with a cost in ticks.
The leg ends: found, partial, no path or over budget.
The route comes back as positions and steps.
Every tick: forward held, jump on a step up, facing the next block.
The current facing is read.
The turn is limited to 30 degrees per tick.
The game's own keys are held; the player walks.
Within half a block of the goal: 'arrived', all keys released.
The line appears in the game log.

routes.name: Plan ahead on long walks
routes.summary: When fewer than 20 steps of route remain and the goal is further, the next stretch is searched while the player keeps walking.
routes.statusWhy: Unit-tested; the 100-block in-game walk (checklist step 21) has never been run.
stepNotes: Twenty or fewer steps remain and the route ends short of the goal.
A search starts from the route's end, not from the player.
It advances one slice per tick.
The leg finishes.
The continuation is appended; the player's place on the route is unchanged.
Keys kept being written on every one of those ticks.

routes.name: Replan when pushed off route
routes.summary: If the player ends up more than 2 blocks from the route, by a teleport or a shove, the bot stops, searches again from where it is, and continues.
routes.statusWhy: Unit-tested; the in-game teleport test (checklist step 16) has never been run. That test is also what would confirm the bot needs no 'server moved you' event.
stepNotes: The player is more than 2 blocks from every nearby route point.
All keys are released once and the old route is dropped.
'off path, repathing' is logged.
A new search starts from the player's position.
The new route replaces the old one.
Walking resumes.

routes.name: Give up when blocked
routes.summary: No progress along the route for 2 seconds triggers a replan; three replans in a row without progress and the bot stops and stands still.
routes.statusWhy: Unit-tested; in-game checklist steps 19 and 20 have never been run.
stepNotes: The player's place on the route has not advanced for 40 ticks.
'stuck, repathing' is logged.
A new search starts from the player.
A fourth replan without progress: it gives up.
Every key is released.
'giving up after 3 repaths without progress' is logged.

routes.name: Stop when goal is unreachable
routes.summary: If a search proves there is no way to the goal, the walk ends at once instead of retrying.
stepNotes: A route is requested.
The search explores everything reachable.
Outcome: no path.
The result comes back with that outcome.
The walk stops; any partial route found is not walked.
'no path to the goal' is logged.

routes.name: Keep walking through menus
routes.summary: Opening the inventory clears the game's held keys; because the bot restates all keys every tick, the walk loses at most one tick.
routes.statusWhy: Confirmed in game on 2026-09-02 with the earlier straight-line walk; not yet re-checked with the route walker (checklist step 15).
stepNotes: A screen opens and the game releases every held key.
The next tick arrives as usual.
The walker runs as on any other tick.
It states the full key set again, remembering nothing.
The keys pass through.
The keys are held again; the walk continues.

routes.name: Stop on leaving the world
routes.summary: Quitting, disconnecting or stepping through a portal mid-walk stops the bot and releases its keys, so nothing is left held.
routes.statusWhy: Checked in both game versions, including the portal case (2026-08-13, 2026-08-14), and covered by the conformance suite. Those in-game runs predate the route walker.
stepNotes: The game's world object changes or disappears.
The next tick carries the new world.
The gate sees a different world than last tick.
It orders the bot to stop.
The walker cancels its search and drops its route.
Every key is released, once.
The release passes through.
No key stays held in the game.
All remembered block kinds are forgotten.
The marked goal is cleared too.
'stopping: client level changed' is logged.
The line appears in the game log.

routes.name: Survive a bot crash
routes.summary: If the bot throws an error, the game carries on: the bot is stopped, its keys released, and it stays silent until the next world load.
routes.statusWhy: Asserted by the conformance suite. Never exercised in a real game, by design: it would need a deliberate crash.
stepNotes: Something inside the bot throws.
The gate catches it; the game's tick loop never sees it.
The error is logged with its stack trace.
The bot is ordered to stop, releasing keys.
The line appears in the game log.
No more ticks are delivered until a world loads, which clears the fault.

routes.name: Preview a route
routes.summary: Press L to search from where you stand to the marked goal without walking; you get a summary line and a text map of the route.
routes.statusWhy: Run in a live client on 2026-08-31, and in both game versions on 2026-09-02.

The click is collected at the end of the tick.
The marked goal is taken; without one the probe says so and stops.
The start is the player's feet position.
The player is turned to face the goal.
A search starts, with the gap jump allowed.
It advances one slice per tick.
Terrain is read through a copy.
Moves are offered and priced.

The route and every visited position come back.
